boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented UCLA rituals, spirit events and long-running community traditions, including one clearly labeled discontinued practice.

cards.title: Spring Sing
cards.subtitle: Annual student music, dance and comedy showcase
cards.notes: Plan for the May show and watch UCLA students present original or arranged musical acts, dance, a cappella and sketch comedy.
cards.short_summary: A one-night UCLA performance tradition that puts student-made acts on a large stage.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA describes Spring Sing as one of its oldest traditions; students perform originally composed, arranged or choreographed musical acts each year.
cards.access_notes: Check Spring Sing’s current event information for attendance and ticket details.

cards.title: Beat ’SC Bonfire and Rally
cards.subtitle: Annual rivalry-week gathering before UCLA–USC football
cards.notes: Join the campus gathering during rivalry week to cheer with student performers and the Bruin community before the USC game.
cards.short_summary: A UCLA rivalry-week rally centered on school spirit and the annual football matchup with USC.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Admissions calls the Beat ’SC Bonfire an annual tradition that brings students, alumni and others together before the rivalry football game against USC.
cards.access_notes: Timing and format vary by football season; confirm current UCLA event details before attending.

cards.title: Dinners for 12 Strangers
cards.subtitle: Alumni-hosted meals that mix students, faculty and alumni
cards.notes: Apply when the program opens for a chance to share a meal and conversation with Bruins you have not met before.
cards.short_summary: A long-running UCLA dinner tradition designed to turn groups of strangers into connections.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni identifies Dinners for 12 Strangers as a tradition since 1968 in which local alumni host students, faculty and fellow alumni.
cards.access_notes: Participation is program-based; consult UCLA Alumni for current application, host and eligibility details.

cards.title: I ♥ UCLA Week
cards.subtitle: May week of Bruin pride and spirit
cards.notes: Look for the May schedule and choose a listed pride or service activity that fits your week on campus.
cards.short_summary: A UCLA-branded week devoted to campus pride and community participation.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni lists I ♥ UCLA Week in May as a week of Bruin pride and spirit celebrating UCLA.
cards.access_notes: Review the current UCLA Alumni calendar for that year’s activities and any participation requirements.

cards.title: 8-Clap Heard Around the World
cards.subtitle: UCLA spirit clap recognized by the True Bruin program
cards.notes: Learn the clap through official spirit programming, then join it at an appropriate UCLA event with the surrounding crowd.
cards.short_summary: A named UCLA crowd-participation ritual included in the True Bruin Traditions Keeper.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s True Bruin Traditions Keeper specifically lists participation in the “8-Clap Heard Around the World” as a UCLA spirit tradition.
cards.access_notes: Use UCLA’s current spirit-event guidance and participate only where invited or customary.

cards.title: Bruin Bash
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week concert hosted on campus
cards.notes: Watch for Welcome Week announcements and attend the student concert at the Los Angeles Tennis Center when scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A beginning-of-year UCLA concert tradition produced for Welcome Week.
cards.evidence_claim: ASUCLA describes Bruin Bash as an annual concert hosted by USAC Campus Events Commission and Cultural Affairs at the beginning of each school year.
cards.access_notes: Check current USAC or UCLA event announcements for lineup, entry rules and scheduling.

cards.title: Rub the Bruin Bear’s Paw
cards.subtitle: Good-luck gesture at the Bruin Bear statue
cards.notes: Before an exam, stop by the Bruin Bear and gently rub its paw as a campus good-luck gesture; respect the statue and nearby visitors.
cards.short_summary: A small, named UCLA exam-season ritual centered on the Bruin Bear statue.
cards.evidence_claim: ASUCLA states that Bruins rub the paw of the bear statue before midterms, finals or whenever they want good luck.
cards.access_notes: The gesture is informal; keep the visit brief and follow any posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Transfer T-Shirt Exchange
cards.subtitle: Transfer-student spirit activity in the True Bruin program
cards.notes: If you are a transfer student, check transition-program announcements and join the exchange only when its current format is offered.
cards.short_summary: A named UCLA transfer-community tradition recognized by the True Bruin program.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s True Bruin Traditions Keeper lists participation in the Transfer T-Shirt Exchange among its UCLA spirit traditions.
cards.access_notes: Availability and eligibility may vary; verify details with New Student & Transition Programs.

cards.title: Carpe Noctem
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation tradition
cards.notes: During New Student Orientation, ask your orientation staff about the current Carpe Noctem activity and follow the program’s instructions.
cards.short_summary: A named orientation-era UCLA tradition included in the True Bruin checklist.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s True Bruin Traditions Keeper lists participation in “Carpe Noctem” at New Student Orientation.
cards.access_notes: This is tied to New Student Orientation; confirm current eligibility and programming with orientation staff.

cards.title: Midnight Yell (Discontinued)
cards.subtitle: Historical finals-week stress-release practice
cards.notes: Treat this as UCLA history rather than an activity: the former midnight finals-week yell was banned over disruption and safety concerns.
cards.short_summary: A documented but discontinued collective finals-week ritual, retained as part of UCLA’s tradition history.
cards.evidence_claim: ASUCLA says Midnight Yell involved finals-week midnight screams and was banned in 2002 because of disruption and safety concerns.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued; do not recreate it. Use quiet, approved finals-week stress-relief resources instead.
